newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia pledges to stay in ATPC.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia pledges to stay in ATPC.

text.p: The director-general of Indonesia's Mining Ministry said on Thursday the country would remain in the Association of Tin Producing Countries (ATPC), but he foresaw no problems if the body dispersed.

"Indonesia pledges to stay in the ATPC, but if the body has to be dispersed, we also don't foresee any problem," Kuntoro Mangkusubroto, director-general of mining in the Mines and Energy Ministry, told Reuters.
Mangkusubroto said the ATPC was useful and Indonesia had no plans to withdraw from the international tin body.
"What we want is only that there shouldn't be any more tin quotas," Mangkusubroto said.
He said the ATPC could be used as a forum for producers and consumers and also a place to exchange view and statistics.
"If the tin body dispersed, Indonesia is ready to enter the free market," he said.
Mangkusubroto said Indonesia had known Australia and Thailand would pull out of the organisation.
"Australia and Thailand have their own interests to keep in mind. We have also doubted whether Brazil would become an ATPC member from the beginning. But we see no problem for Indonesia," he said.
